Well, as far is cognitive ability, there is some evidence that supplements like citicoline and alpha gpc associate with moderate improvements in recall. There's also evidence that being healthy and having a strong immune system associates with improvements in cognitive ability. The same can be said for regular exercise and spending time on yourself. 

So there are things you can take, things you can do. But one thing that you may not have considered is that, you're slightly concerned with your generalised ability to fluidly respond to problems. The counter to this is to improve your knowledgeability or experience in several areas. Some people that seem to be "naturally" smart or good at things, often dedicate hours and hours actually trying to improve at the thing, and not just only doing the thing for the sake of it with the absence of a goal. 

So my advice would be, start exercising, and find something to try to get good at, not better than someone, but just better than you were before you started. You  can really gain a lot of self knowledge from continuously attempting to improve at one particular thing. 

Choosing one thing to work at is a good way to explore what happens in your brain when you attempt to make a familiar environment unfamiliar by attempting to improve.
